investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (used by the Kata peer-pods runtime) reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm — meaning the allocatable quota for that resource is at zero or fully consumed by existing workloads. The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes. With no schedulable node, the pod remained Pending for 131–144 seconds until the eval timeout fired, producing an empty evidence object and a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on both capable nodes — existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have claimed all allocatable VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

[Likely] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity went NotReady or was cordoned/drained between the last passing run and this eval, reducing the effective pool from a previously sufficient count to only 2 nodes with zero remaining quota.

[Possible] The remote-agent pod spec's node affinity or node selector was recently tightened (e.g., requiring a label only present on the two kata-capable nodes), causing the 4 general-purpose nodes to be excluded — but this would be a pre-existing condition unless a config change occurred.

[Possible] A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from other users or parallel eval runs) exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both nodes just before this eval ran, causing a transient capacity crunch.

[Lower confidence] The cluster's peer-pods provider (cloud VM quota, peer-pod daemon capacity, or the kata-agent resource plugin) hit an external limit that caused the node-level extended resource count to drop to zero without a node going offline.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 and no pods currently consuming those slots, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion — it would point instead to a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec or a node label mismatch.

If the remote-agent-create eval passed on an immediate re-run without any node or workload changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent burst of requests that has since cleared) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the cause would be isolated to the create path rather than a cluster-wide scheduling constraint.

If the four non-kata nodes showed the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and the pod's affinity rules were satisfied by them, the diagnosis would shift to a node selector or taint mismatch rather than resource exhaustion.
If a cluster event log showed a kata-capable node going NotReady after the last passing eval run, the cause would be node loss rather than quota exhaustion on healthy nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm available capacity on the production cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct pre-condition failure rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a remote-agent-node-pool-health check that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are Ready and correctly labeled, catching node loss or label drift independently of the creation flow.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes pod phase and scheduler message as structured evidence fields (e.g., podPhase, schedulerReason), enabling contract assertions on scheduling health rather than relying solely on the timeout message string.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes show Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none match the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent creation step, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be absent and all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the pod's nodeSelector or affinity rules require the kata.peerpods.io/vm label or a related taint/toleration that only 2 of 6 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. This is a contributing structural constraint visible in the scheduler message.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed to terminate agent pods, those pods would continue to hold VM resource slots, starving new scheduling attempts.

Cluster under-provisioning for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class: the total VM capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent or back-to-back eval runs, especially if the feature's staleAfterMinutes=20 window triggers frequent re-runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (used by the Kata peer-pods runtime) reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm — meaning the allocatable quota for that resource is at zero or fully consumed by existing workloads. The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules, which restrict remote-agent pods to kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes. With no schedulable node, the pod remained Pending for 131–144 seconds until the eval timeout fired, producing an empty evidence object and a complete contract validation failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 131s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-02T23:50:37.416Z — confirms the scheduling failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, endedAt 2026-07-02T23:53:04.167Z — all three checks across the remote-agents feature share the same root scheduler error.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod is never scheduled, no VM ID or state is ever returned to the probe.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=136595 — the probe ran for ~136 s before failing, consistent with the scheduler's 131 s unscheduled duration plus eval overhead.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on both capable nodes — existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have claimed all allocatable VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

[Likely] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity went NotReady or was cordoned/drained between the last passing run and this eval, reducing the effective pool from a previously sufficient count to only 2 nodes with zero remaining quota.

[Possible] The remote-agent pod spec's node affinity or node selector was recently tightened (e.g., requiring a label only present on the two kata-capable nodes), causing the 4 general-purpose nodes to be excluded — but this would be a pre-existing condition unless a config change occurred.

[Possible] A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from other users or parallel eval runs) exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both nodes just before this eval ran, causing a transient capacity crunch.

[Lower confidence] The cluster's peer-pods provider (cloud VM quota, peer-pod daemon capacity, or the kata-agent resource plugin) hit an external limit that caused the node-level extended resource count to drop to zero without a node going offline.

If the remote-agent-create eval passed on an immediate re-run without any node or workload changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent burst of requests that has since cleared) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the cause would be isolated to the create path rather than a cluster-wide scheduling constraint.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes pod phase and scheduler message as structured evidence fields (e.g., podPhase, schedulerReason), enabling contract assertions on scheduling health rather than relying solely on the timeout message string.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes show Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm) and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none match the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent creation step, causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be absent and all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 144s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150570 — the check ran for ~150s, consistent with the scheduler's unschedulable timeout window before the runner surfaced the error.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs or peer-pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the pod's nodeSelector or affinity rules require the kata.peerpods.io/vm label or a related taint/toleration that only 2 of 6 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. This is a contributing structural constraint visible in the scheduler message.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed to terminate agent pods, those pods would continue to hold VM resource slots, starving new scheduling attempts.

Cluster under-provisioning for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class: the total VM capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent or back-to-back eval runs, especially if the feature's staleAfterMinutes=20 window triggers frequent re-runs.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod matched more than 2 nodes, the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' constraint would be the sole bottleneck rather than a combination of affinity mismatch and resource exhaustion.
If no existing remote-agent pods were found on the cluster, leaked pods would be ruled out as a contributing cause of the resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that polls kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the production-api cluster nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add a remote-agent-pod-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval run's withCleanup phase, catching resource leaks before they exhaust VM capacity.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that asserts the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity matches at least N nodes in the cluster, catching configuration drift that concentrates scheduling onto too few nodes.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between a scheduling timeout and an application-level creation failure, so future scheduling errors are immediately identifiable without requiring manual log inspection.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the runtime eval never reached the point of collecting any evidence — leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity (resource exhausted), and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption is also unavailable — no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime. The same scheduling failure independently caused remote-agent-create (131 s stuck) and remote-agent-state (144 s stuck) to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000 — the observed latency of 146751 ms is well under the outage threshold, so this is a scheduling failure, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This directly matches the scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

CONTRIBUTING — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective scheduling pool is limited to those 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

SECONDARY — no preemption victims available: no lower-priority pods exist on the 2 eligible nodes that could be evicted to free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, meaning the scheduler cannot self-heal through preemption.

LESS LIKELY — a recent cluster scaling event or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the demand level; no node-count or scaling evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

LESS LIKELY — a concurrent surge in remote agent creation by other workloads consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before the eval pods were scheduled; no concurrent-workload evidence is present in the packet.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both nodes eligible for remote agent pods (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state). This is the earliest violated constraint in the provisioning chain.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent node affinity/selector pool
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded from scheduling by the pod's node affinity or node selector, reducing the effective scheduling pool to 2 nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same underlying scheduling error, as recorded in sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-state. The feature registry at lines 183-185 shows remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true checks, making this a degraded-feature signal.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval runner branch
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. The scheduling failure prevents the probe from ever collecting the required evidence fields defined in the expected-output contract.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266-270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message. All five are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence) because the pod never started and no agent response was produced.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the production cluster to confirm current VM slot utilization and identify which pods are consuming all available slots.
Determine whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool can be expanded by adding more peer-pod-capable nodes or increasing the VM slot limit on existing nodes to restore scheduling headroom.
Check for any leaked or stuck remote agent pods from previous eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads; terminate them if found.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to confirm that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes are intended targets, and assess whether additional nodes should be labeled to widen the scheduling pool.

Monitor the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks after any capacity remediation to confirm all three return to passing status; remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true checks (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 183-184) and their failure contributes to the feature's degraded-after-failures=1 threshold.

Note that this is an eval-observed infrastructure signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet. Confirm with platform/infrastructure teams whether production remote agent provisioning is also impacted before escalating as a user-facing incident.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient at the time of the recorded failure (failed-check.timing).

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling failure across sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, and the primary check is reproducible as a cluster-level condition.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and current allocations
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Running kubectl describe nodes filtered to kata.peerpods.io/vm will show Allocatable vs. allocated counts on the 2 eligible nodes, directly confirming or refuting the resource exhaustion diagnosis from failed-check.message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm in the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifying which pods hold the VM slots will reveal whether the pool is legitimately saturated by active workloads or whether leaked/stuck pods are holding capacity that should have been released.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would be contradicted and a different scheduling or API bug would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was freed) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the failing pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause such as a misconfigured resource request in the agent creation path.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the cause would be isolated to the runtime probe rather than shared cluster capacity.
If the cluster has more than 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes at the time of the failure, the '2 Insufficient' count in the message would be inaccurate and the diagnosis would need revision.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure-capacity check rather than a timeout inside the agent lifecycle checks.
Add a cluster node inventory eval that asserts the count of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes meets a minimum threshold, catching node loss or label drift before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a stuck-pod detection eval that scans for remote agent pods in Pending/Unschedulable state older than a configurable threshold and reports them as a separate infrastructure health signal.

Consider adding a latency-band eval for remote-agent-create that distinguishes scheduling latency from API latency, enabling faster triage when the failure is in the Kubernetes layer vs. the agent API layer.
